previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with long-standing epilepsy, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted after experiencing breakthrough seizures during a dialysis session. He had not taken his antiepileptic medications for approximately one week due to running out, which was identified as the likely cause. He was restarted on levetiracetam and oxcarbazepine and remained seizure-free. A chest X-ray revealed findings consistent with multifocal pneumonia, and he was treated with a five-day course of azithromycin. His mental status improved from initial confusion to baseline, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to maintain medication adherence, complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with neurology and primary care.

clopidogrel (plavix), which you will take once daily each.

future medical appointments are listed below for you.  Please be 
sure to attend your follow up appointments to ensure your 
symptoms resolve with your treatments.

more than 3 lbs.

We wish you the best with you health.

Sincerely,
Your ___ Care Team
